events.title: Deadly earthquake strikes Charleston
events.description: One of the strongest earthquakes ever recorded on the U.S. East Coast shook Charleston, South Carolina, and caused widespread destruction and loss of life.
events.significance: The quake showed that serious seismic risk exists far from the tectonic plate boundaries. It still shapes how scientists think about earthquake hazards in the eastern United States.

events.title: Birth of Maria Montessori
events.description: Maria Montessori was born in Chiaravalle, Italy. She became one of Italy's first female physicians and later developed a new approach to educating children.
events.significance: Her child-centered, hands-on Montessori method is used in schools around the world today.

events.title: Triple Entente formed
events.description: Britain and Russia signed an agreement that settled their rivalries in Asia. This joined them with France in a loose alliance known as the Triple Entente.
events.significance: The Entente helped divide Europe into two rival blocs, and these blocs went to war in 1914.

events.title: Staged Gleiwitz radio station incident
events.description: Nazi operatives staged a fake Polish attack on a German radio station at Gleiwitz, near the Polish border. They presented it as provocation by Poland.
events.significance: Germany used the incident as a pretext to invade Poland the next day, which began World War II in Europe.

events.title: Death of Diana, Princess of Wales
events.description: Diana died after a car crash in a Paris tunnel. She was 36. Her death set off an outpouring of grief in Britain and around the world.
events.significance: Her death prompted a national reckoning over the monarchy, media intrusion and public mourning. Her humanitarian legacy endures.
